assertions.name: descent_block_scalar_is_dominant_qgevrey_driver
assertions.source: T_k=A_k+q^(2k)B_k at q_0: multiplier slope -> 2 ln q_0 (q-Gevrey, 13.7% below target at n=30, converging from below); disabling the q^(2k) scalar drops the slope to ~1/3 (descent block dominant, content monomials secondary); envelope ratio rises in the tail. q-Gevrey class confirmed; descent scalar is the dominant driver.

description: Lever-1 W9 (z2bn follow-up): spectral reading of the descent-set transfer operator T_k = A_k + q^(2k) B_k (W6) evaluated numerically at the muon-canonical q_0. (S1) q=1: Z_n = I(n), per-level log-multiplier ~ (1/2)ln n (Gevrey-1/2). (S2) q_0: multiplier LINEAR in n, tail slope matches 2 ln q_0 within 2% (log Z_n ~ quadratic => q-Gevrey), reproducing the alien-calculus review's measured class change as a spectral statement. (S3) DECOMPOSITION: disabling the q^(2k) descent scalar (content monomials kept) drops the multiplier slope from ~0.18 to ~0.056 — the descent-block level scalar is the DOMINANT (~2/3) contributor to the q-Gevrey rate; the residual comes from the content weighting q^(j-i), itself quadratic-log (max content n(n-1)/2), so this is an honest decomposition, not a sole-cause claim. Both ingredients vanish at q=1 (Gevrey-1/2). Envelope ratio log S^bal/log(p(n) prod[k]_q0) rises in the tail n>=10 (no plateau, slowly toward 1). Exact operator, 50-dps mpmath; no fit; no wiring; EXPLORATORY.
